incidents-bot: INCIDENT OPENED — routing anomalies detected.
incidents-bot: Priority: P1, symptom: 5xx misroutes from eu-west -> us-central causing degraded SLA for EU customers. Pager: @alex (oncall). Links: https://ops.redwood/internal/incidents/2109123456
alex (oncall): acknow — jumping in. first pass: confirm impact. amanda, any customer reports?
amanda (support): seeing ~12 tickets in last 10m from eu customers. Some report hallucinated model outputs or timeouts, others say responses returned from us region with longer latency. cc @mira
mira (sre): looking at router metrics — sudden spike in route-fallback events at 2026-03-15T10:04:12Z. correlates with a surge in eu-west tail latency. adding traces.
tara (eng-runtime): I'm on model routing dashboard. There's a spike of requests being routed to fallback-model-v2 instead of primary-v5 for EU tier. policy logs show a region-evacuation rule triggered for eu-west at 10:03:58Z (evacuation -> route to us-central).
kevin (eng-platform): did we kick an autoscale or maintenance? I triggered a rolling kernel bump on a small eu pool at 09:55 but that should be isolated. checking control plane events.
alex (oncall): quick mitigation: can we temporarily disable region-evacuation rule to stop spillover? risk: might overload degraded hosts. pros/cons?
tara (eng-runtime): mitigation plan A: pause evacuation rule, enable local degraded-fallback to model-compat (quantized variant) in eu. Plan B: if evicting causes overload, route to dedicated low-latency reserve (dedicated-reserve-eu) with throttling.
mira (sre): I'm watching node CPU + queue lengths. eu-west has ~30% CPU but a few nodes show NVMe errors and dropped health checks around 10:03:50. That likely triggered the evacuation. Logs: 
```
[10:03:49] node-12 healthcheck: disk read error, io(2) timeout
[10:03:50] node-12 kube-probe: failing liveness
[10:03:51] router: node-12 removed from pool, evacuation policy applied
```
kevin (eng-platform): aha — disk errors. Not a network blip. I can repro the NVMe SMART spike; looks like node-12's drive entered readonly then flapped. Opening host ticket.
amanda (support): customers impacted: 9 high-priority, 21 medium. CS frag saying some customers saw responses from wrong locale. We should include a customer impact blurb for the post-incident notes.
alex (oncall): ok immediate steps: 1) tara/mira implement temporary pause of evacuation rule (if safe) 2) tara route traffic to dedicated-reserve-eu with 10% throttling 3) kevin isolate node-12 and start remediation 4) amanda compile affected customers. I'll coordinate exec updates. Ready?
tara (eng-runtime): executing step 1 now — disabling evacuation rule (console):
```
# patching routing-policies/eu-evac
PATCH /api/v1/policies/routing-policies/eu-evac
{"enabled":false}
```
tara (eng-runtime): step 1 done. waiting 30s for policy sync.
mira (sre): I see route-fallback events drop by ~85% after policy disabled. good. node queues still slightly elevated.
tara (eng-runtime): step 2: creating a temporary route:
```
route: eu-public -> dedicated-reserve-eu priority=high throttle=10%
```
tara (eng-runtime): route applied. feeding 25% of new connections to reserve initially.
deploy-bot: deploy started: route-change-v2026-0315-1 by tara (eng-runtime). CI checks passed.
kevin (eng-platform): isolated node-12 from cluster and marked drive for replacement. Will monitor for cascade. I don't see other NVMe anomalies.
alex (oncall): good work. mira — collect relevant traces and logs for the RCA thread. ask: did fallback model selection contribute? were requests routed to a fallback that is incompatible with EU prompt templates?
mira (sre): traces show most misroutes were due to policy evacuation, not model mismatch. however ~12% of sessions routed to fallback-model-v2 which has different tokenization leading to odd outputs. that's likely why some customers saw hallucinations. we should mark that as contributing factor.
tara (eng-runtime): why did router choose fallback-model-v2? policy graph: evacuation -> compatibility-matrix -> select first compatible variant. For a subset of EU model variants, v5 not available, v2 was picked because quantization profile matched. we need to tighten compatibility check.
kevin (eng-platform): short-term mitigations: 1) revert compatibility fallback order for eu to prefer quantized-compat with same tokenizer 2) add guard: don't select model with incompatible tokenizer for EU lang packs. I can push a hotfix to policy service.
amanda (support): I'm preparing a customer update: ETA for full mitigation?
alex (oncall): ETA 35-45m for full stable state. we'll send interim note in 15m. amanda, please include TL;DR: some responses came from us-central and a minority used an older model variant causing formatting differences. Apologize and say engineering is on it.
mira (sre): collecting artifacts: router policy logs, node-12 SMART logs, route-change events, per-tenant trace samples. saving to /mnt/rca-artifacts/2109123456/ (internal link: https://ops.redwood/internal/artifacts/2109123456)
tara (eng-runtime): I'm adding a hypothesis tracker in-thread:
- H1: NVMe/host failure triggered evacuation -> spillover -> misroutes (primary root).
- H2: Compatibility matrix allowed tokenizer-incompatible fallback (secondary contributor).
- H3: Control-plane rolling kernel bump overlapped with health flaps (unlikely but possible).
ara (kevin): tagging H1 as supported (NVMe logs confirm). H2 has partial support from trace tokenization diffs. H3: logs show kernel bump completed earlier and unrelated. mark unlikely.
alex (oncall): good. timeline summary for postmortem start (timestamps UTC):
- 09:55:00 patch: rolling kernel bump initiated (control-plane)
- 10:03:49 node-12 nvme read errors begin
- 10:03:50 kube liveness failures on node-12
- 10:03:51 router evacuation policy removes node-12
- 10:03:58 evacuation policy triggers region-evac for eu-west
- 10:04:05 surge of route-fallback events -> routed users to us-central and fallback-model-v2
- 10:05:20 incident pager fires, tickets start arriving
- 10:08:00 evacuation rule disabled (mitigation)
- 10:12:30 dedicated-reserve-eu route applied and throttling active
- 10:18:00 route-fallback events down to baseline
amanda (support): draft for interim customer message: "We're aware of an issue affecting European users, some requests were served from a different region and a small number used an older model variant. Engineers are mitigating; we expect stabilisation within the hour. We're collecting logs and will follow up with a detailed post-incident report." suggest we include impacted tenant IDs.
tara (eng-runtime): note for RCA: we'll need to add a policy safeguard: 'tokenizer_compat_required' flag and a rate-based guard to avoid cascading evacuations for single-node disk issues. I'll open PR after handoff.
kevin (eng-platform): host remediation: node-12 drive replacement scheduled + SMART monitoring alert threshold lowered. also adding a short-term control-plane check to avoid auto-evacuating entire region when <X% nodes failing.
mira (sre): adding links to raw traces and policy logs in the artifact bucket.
deploy-bot: deploy complete: route-change-v2026-0315-1 succeeded.
alex (oncall): switching to 2nd oncall handoff in 30m. @mira you're owning initial RCA doc, @tara you'll own policy changes, @kevin host remediation. amanda owner for customer comms. I'll post an executive summary once we confirm final counts.
amanda (support): will send interim update in 10m. collecting impacted tenant IDs now.
incidents-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: Mitigation applied, status: stabilizing. Add updates to incident page: https://ops.redwood/internal/incidents/2109123456/updates
alex (oncall): closing live coordination here. keep updates in this thread for RCA artifact collection. we'll reconvene if any regressions. thanks all :thumbsup:
